title: QUESTION TAGS & INTERROGATIVES
notes:
✓ Question tag → a short question added to the end of a statement to confirm information, seek agreement, or check whether something is true.

✓ You are Ethiopian, aren't you?
✓ She can swim, can't she?

✓ Interrogatives → question words or structures used to ask for information.

◆ Who → person
◆ What → thing/information
◆ Which → choice
◆ Where → place
◆ When → time
◆ Why → reason
◆ Whose → possession
◆ How → manner/condition

title: BASIC QUESTION TAG RULE
notes:
✓ Positive statement → negative tag.
✓ You are ready, aren't you?
✓ She likes coffee, doesn't she?

✓ Negative statement → positive tag.
✓ You aren't ready, are you?
✓ She doesn't like coffee, does she?

✓ Golden rule → Positive ↔ Negative.

title: USE THE AUXILIARY VERB
notes:
✓ The question tag normally uses the same auxiliary/modal as the statement.

✓ She is studying, isn't she?
✓ They have finished, haven't they?
✓ He can drive, can't he?
✓ You will come, won't you?
✓ We should leave, shouldn't we?

✓ The main verb does not normally appear in the tag.

title: QUESTION TAGS WITH DO / DOES / DID
notes:
✓ When there is no auxiliary in the statement, use do, does, or did.

✓ You like English, don't you?
✓ She likes English, doesn't she?
✓ They play football, don't they?
✓ He went home, didn't he?
✓ She studied hard, didn't she?

◆ Present simple → do/does.
◆ Past simple → did.

title: QUESTION TAGS WITH BE
notes:
✓ Use the appropriate form of BE in the tag.

✓ He is a student, isn't he?
✓ They are ready, aren't they?
✓ She was late, wasn't she?
✓ You were there, weren't you?

✓ Negative statement → positive tag.
✓ He isn't ready, is he?
✓ They weren't late, were they?

title: QUESTION TAGS WITH PERFECT TENSES
notes:
✓ Use have/has/had according to the tense.

✓ She has finished, hasn't she?
✓ They have arrived, haven't they?
✓ He had left, hadn't he?
✓ You haven't seen him, have you?

◆ Present perfect → has/have.
◆ Past perfect → had.

title: QUESTION TAGS WITH MODALS
notes:
✓ Use the same modal in the tag.

✓ He can swim, can't he?
✓ She could help, couldn't she?
✓ They will come, won't they?
✓ You would agree, wouldn't you?
✓ We should study, shouldn't we?
✓ He must leave, mustn't he?

✓ Structure → statement + , + modal + pronoun?

title: SPECIAL CASE: I AM
notes:
✓ With a positive statement using 'I am', the standard question tag is 'aren't I?'

✓ I am late, aren't I?
✓ I am invited, aren't I?

✓ With a negative statement:
✓ I am not late, am I?

✓ 'Aren't I?' is the standard tag form in this special construction.

title: NEGATIVE MEANING WORDS
notes:
✓ Some words have negative meaning, so they usually take a positive tag.

✓ Nobody called, did they?
✓ Nothing happened, did it?
✓ No one knows, do they?
✓ He never lies, does he?
✓ She hardly speaks, does she?

✓ Words such as nobody, no one, nothing, never, hardly, rarely, and scarcely give the statement a negative meaning.

title: INDEFINITE PRONOUNS IN TAGS
notes:
✓ With words such as everyone, everybody, someone, somebody, nobody, and no one, 'they' is commonly used in the tag.

✓ Everyone is ready, aren't they?
✓ Somebody called, didn't they?
✓ Nobody came, did they?
✓ No one knows, do they?

✓ Singular indefinite pronoun + they is natural and widely used in modern English.

title: IMPERATIVE QUESTION TAGS
notes:
✓ Commands and requests can use special tags.

✓ Open the door, will you?
✓ Don't be late, will you?
✓ Let's go, shall we?
✓ Have a seat, won't you?

✓ 'Let's...' → shall we?
✓ Let's start, shall we?

✓ Commands often use will you?, would you?, won't you?, or can you?, depending on meaning and politeness.

title: AGREEMENT & EXPECTATION
notes:
✓ Question tags can confirm information or invite agreement.

✓ It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
✓ You know the answer, don't you?

✓ The speaker often expects the listener to agree.

✓ A falling intonation usually suggests the speaker expects confirmation.
✓ A rising intonation can show genuine uncertainty.

title: INTERROGATIVES: WHO & WHOM
notes:
✓ Who → asks about a person, especially the subject.

✓ Who called you?
→ Dawit called me.

✓ Who did you see?
→ I saw Dawit.

✓ Whom → formal form used for the object.
✓ Whom did you invite?

✓ In everyday English, 'who' is commonly used instead of 'whom'.

title: WHAT & WHICH
notes:
✓ What → asks about information or an unspecified choice.
✓ What is your name?
✓ What do you want?

✓ Which → asks someone to choose from a limited or known set.
✓ Which color do you prefer, red or blue?
✓ Which book is yours?

✓ WHAT → open/general choice.
✓ WHICH → limited/specific choice.

title: WHERE, WHEN & WHY
notes:
✓ Where → place/location.
✓ Where do you live?

✓ When → time.
✓ When does the class start?

✓ Why → reason.
✓ Why are you late?

✓ Quick memory:
WHERE = place.
WHEN = time.
WHY = reason.

title: WHOSE
notes:
✓ Whose → asks about possession or ownership.

✓ Whose book is this?
→ It is Dawit's book.

✓ Whose phone did you take?
→ I took John's phone.

⚠ Whose ≠ who's.

✓ whose → possession.
✓ who's → who is / who has.

title: HOW & HOW + ADJECTIVE/ADVERB
notes:
✓ How → asks about manner, condition, or method.
✓ How are you?
✓ How did you solve it?

✓ How + adjective/adverb → asks about degree or manner.

✓ How old are you? → age
✓ How far is the school? → distance
✓ How long is the lesson? → duration/length
✓ How often do you study? → frequency
✓ How fast can he run? → speed
✓ How well do you know her? → degree/quality

title: HOW MUCH & HOW MANY
notes:
✓ How much → uncountable nouns or amount.
✓ How much water do you need?
✓ How much money do you have?

✓ How many → plural countable nouns.
✓ How many books do you have?
✓ How many students are there?

✓ MUCH → uncountable.
✓ MANY → plural countable.

title: YES/NO QUESTIONS
notes:
✓ Yes/no questions normally begin with an auxiliary or modal verb.

✓ Are you ready?
✓ Do you like English?
✓ Did she arrive?
✓ Have they finished?
✓ Can he swim?
✓ Will you come?

✓ Structure → Auxiliary/Modal + subject + main verb/complement?

✓ Do + you + like + coffee?
✓ Can + she + drive?

title: WH-QUESTIONS
notes:
✓ Basic structure → WH-word + auxiliary + subject + main verb?

✓ Where do you live?
✓ Why did she leave?
✓ What are they doing?
✓ When will you arrive?

✓ If the WH-word is the subject, do not add do/does/did.

✓ Who called you?
✓ What happened?

❌ Who did call you? → normally unnecessary in a neutral question.
✓ Who called you?

title: SUBJECT VS OBJECT QUESTIONS
notes:
✓ Subject question → asks who/what performs the action.
✓ Who broke the window?
→ John broke it.

✓ Object question → asks who/what receives the action.
✓ Who did John call?
→ He called Mary.

✓ Subject question → usually no do/does/did.
✓ Object question → normally uses do/does/did in simple tenses.

title: INDIRECT QUESTIONS
notes:
✓ Indirect questions are more polite or formal and use statement word order.

✓ Direct → Where is the station?
✓ Indirect → Could you tell me where the station is?

✓ Direct → What does he want?
✓ Indirect → Do you know what he wants?

⚠ Do not use question word order inside the indirect question.

❌ Do you know where is he?
✓ Do you know where he is?

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ She is ready, doesn't she?
✓ She is ready, isn't she?

❌ He likes football, isn't he?
✓ He likes football, doesn't he?

❌ They went home, weren't they?
✓ They went home, didn't they?

❌ Nobody came, didn't they?
✓ Nobody came, did they?

❌ Who did call you?
✓ Who called you?

❌ Do you know where is the bank?
✓ Do you know where the bank is?

❌ How many money do you have?
✓ How much money do you have?

✓ Always identify the auxiliary, polarity, and whether the WH-word is the subject or object.

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ QUESTION TAGS

✓ Positive → negative tag.
You are ready, aren't you?

✓ Negative → positive tag.
You aren't ready, are you?

✓ No auxiliary → do/does/did.
She likes it, doesn't she?

✓ Modal → same modal.
He can swim, can't he?

✓ Perfect → have/has/had.
They have finished, haven't they?

✓ I am → aren't I?
I am late, aren't I?

✓ Let's → shall we?
Let's go, shall we?

◆ INTERROGATIVES

✓ Who → person.
✓ What → thing/information.
✓ Which → limited choice.
✓ Where → place.
✓ When → time.
✓ Why → reason.
✓ Whose → possession.
✓ How → manner/condition.
✓ How much → uncountable amount.
✓ How many → countable number.

✓ Golden rule → For question tags, copy the auxiliary and reverse positive/negative. For interrogatives, choose the question word according to the information you need.
